Question: How are our smartphones notifying phone scammers that it's a good time to call since we've just hung up and will likely respond to rather than ignore a ring?
Answer: It’s possible that it’s simply a perception, but I doubt it: the “I was JUST on the phone!” experience when hearing a ring is way too common. My best guess is that their calling algorithms simply repeat call every 30 seconds or so every time they get a busy signal. Maybe if we charged a penny per “sorry, busy!” call we could eliminate half the scam calls that plague us. People would initially be mad at having to pay for what happens when they hit busies themselves, but the combo of relief from scammers AND a reduction in base phone # home rates would more than make up for it.
